title: Unstructured Grounding: Chunking Knowledge in Data 360

steps.prompt: An Agentforce service agent must be grounded on PDF manuals and related Account files via Data 360 unstructured / search capabilities. Retrieval quality is poor, some PDFs never chunk, and stakeholders also want near-real-time file answers. Which approach best balances semantic coherence, product limits, and freshness?

options.label: Use section-aware chunking (250–500 tokens) on text PDFs, and leverage direct Agent Actions for real-time CRM file retrieval
options.rationale: Chunking between 250–500 tokens preserves semantic coherence. Complex tables should be preprocessed, and real-time CRM files are best queried via direct Agent Actions rather than waiting on periodic search index rebuilds.

options.label: Embed each entire multi-page PDF as a single comprehensive vector to preserve cross-paragraph context across the document
options.distractorAntipattern: Monolithic document embeddings exceed token limits, dilute retrieval similarity, and cause severe hallucination.
options.rationale: Single-vector document embeddings dilute semantic relevance, exceed embedding model context windows, and prevent precise chunk retrieval.

options.label: Ingest table-dense PDF manuals directly into unstructured search and enable automated OCR layout recognition in Data Cloud
options.distractorAntipattern: Data Cloud unstructured chunking does not reliably parse complex multi-column tables or dense tabular data without structured preprocessing.
options.rationale: Complex tabular data cannot be reliably indexed by standard unstructured text chunkers, resulting in skipped chunks and corrupted answers.

options.label: Rely entirely on Data Cloud search index re-indexing to expose newly uploaded Account attachments to Agentforce instantly
options.distractorAntipattern: Data Cloud vector indexing operates asynchronously and cannot deliver instantaneous grounding on newly attached files.
options.rationale: Vector search index updates are asynchronous batch processes and cannot guarantee sub-minute freshness for newly created record attachments.
